dct_description_sm: The long-term objective of this project is to establish a monitoring program to understand the temporal and spatial trends of microplastic particles and their plastic associated additives in the Arctic wildlife by implementing standardized microplastic methods to assess ingested plastic pieces in the guts of lake trout, building on a pan-Arctic effort to improve our understanding of plastic in fish species, contributing data on plastic additives (including UV stabilizers and chlorinated paraffins) that are present in traditional foods to partners that are interested in understanding human exposure to these contaminants, and contributing data to the current Arctic Councils Arctic Monitoring and Assessment Programs (AMAP) Litter and Microplastic Expert Group (LMEG) relating to the toxicity of plastic related and derived contaminants in the Arctic. Short-term objectives:measure the ingested plastic particles in Yukon lake trout and establish a baseline dataset for these emerging contaminants in an Arctic freshwater food web; determine if very small plastic particles are present in the muscle tissue of Yukon lake trout and establish a baseline dataset for these emerging contaminants; measure the levels of benzotriazole UV stabilizers (BZT-UVs), a group of plastic additives, in Yukon lake trout and establish a baseline dataset for these emerging contaminants in an Arctic freshwater food web;measure the levels of chlorinated paraffins, a group of contaminants associated with plastics, in Yukon lake trout and establish a baseline dataset for these emerging contaminants in an Arctic freshwater food web; andinvestigate the correlations between the levels of plastic additives, ingested plastics and plastic particles in lake trout muscle, as an indicator of plastic pollution exposure via ingestion.This research program will help to elucidate and reduce the exposure risks of Arctic fish and humans to plastic associated contaminants. The results will also help to evaluate the role of plastics as a vector of these contaminants in the Arctic food web.
dct_subject_sm: Health sciences and contaminants -> Perfluorinated alkylated substances
dct_title_s: Microplastics and plastic additives in Yukon Lake Trout
